newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian oil demand to nearly double in 10 yrs - IOC.
newsitem.headline: Indian oil demand to nearly double in 10 yrs - IOC.

text.p: India's annual petroleum consumption is expected to reach a level of over 150 million tonnes by the year 2006-2007 from a current 81 million tonnes, a a senior oil industry official said.

R.K. Narang, chairman of Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOC) told an aviation seminar in the western Indian coastal resort of Goa that consumption of aviation turbine fuel would reach 3.2 million tonnes per annum by 2006-2007 against a current two million tonnes.

To meet the growing demand of petroleum products in India, it has been projected that an investment of 3,000 billion rupees would be needed in the area of crude oil exploration and production, refining and downstream marketing facilities, Narang was quoted as saying.
Narang comments, at the 6th International Aviation Seminar organised by IOC which opened on Thursday, were contained in an IOC statement. State-owned IOC is India's biggest refiner.
Delegates from 25 countries are attending the two-day meeting, it said.

Narang said IOC, which meets over 67 percent of the country's fuel requirements from its 96 aviation fuel stations, has drawn up a comprehensive plan to set up additional refuelling facilities to cover even new feeder routers of various airlines.

He said that with aviation fuel accounting for nearly 30 percent of the operating costs of an airline, there was a clear case for airline operators to optimise the use of aviation fuels by adopting various conservation methods such as improvement in airframe design and development, besides aero-engine and operations improvements.
